newsitem.title: JORDAN: Palestinians plan to buy up Jerusalem property.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians plan to buy up Jerusalem property.

text.p: Leading Palestinian businessmen said on Wednesday they plan to set up a multi-million dollar firm to buy and develop Arab property in East Jerusalem and prevent it from falling into Israeli hands.

Abdul-Majid Shoman, chairman of Jordan's heavyweight Arab Bank and one of three businessmen behind the idea, said it aimed to provide funds for improved housing for Arabs and to revitalise the eastern sector of the city.

Investors said the project could halt Arab emigration because of economic hardship and also prevent Jewish groups from buying up land in East Jerusalem. Israel annexed the area after capturing it in 1967 although that has not been internationally recognised.
The three businessmen, representing some of the wealthiest expatriate Palestinians, say only firm plans can challenge Israel's stepped-up construction of Jewish settlements around East Jerusalem.
Israeli bulldozers last month started breaking ground to build more Jewish housing on the outskirts of East Jerusalem, provoking violence and widespread Palestinian anger.
But Shoman said the plan also made business sense.

"This is a secure investment which is to do with property and constuction and there will be income...this is investment not a donation, an investment with income which I think will give a high return to investors," Shoman said.

The company's ventures would include housing and hotels. It would also renovate existing property and buy prime real estate. Shoman said the company would have a high rate of return because real estate in Jerusalem was in demand by Jordanian and other Arab investors.
"The holding company will be a commercial investment firm with a fund and a shareholding company with its profits going to its shareholders," Shoman told Reuters.
"We hope the initial capital will be not less than $100 to $200 million or even more if our brothers in Arab states contribute to this project," Shoman said.

Shoman said a meeting hosted by him and two other leading Palestinian businessmen Munib al-Masri and Hasib al-Sabbagh next Saturday in Amman would get commitments to proceed with the company's registration ahead of electing a board of directors.
About 250 potential Palestinian expatriate and local investors, including top Jordanian and Palestinian banks and firms, will be presented with the charter of the company on Saturday.
Shareholders will be asked to pay initially 20 percent of the capital of the firm, which is expected to begin business shortly after it is launched on Saturday, Shoman said.
"Its objective is to help Palestinians to either sell their property or land in Jerusalem and its environment and other property in Palestinian land," Shoman said.

Asked if Israel would put obstacles, Shoman said: "Why would Israel put obstacles...this property which will be bought will be Arab property and its owners are Arab and it will not breach the laws exisiting."
Shoman said Arab investors should have acted earlier to set up such a company to bolster economic activity in Arab East Jerusalem and prevent Israel from tightening its grip.
"We have not done enough...we should have taken note of this matter before and supported citizens of Jerusalem and supported them to stay on their land," Shoman said.
